narrative:
The model estimates you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, the school has decided this risk is high enough to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you might fail is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushes the model toward expecting you to fail. Among students who passed, having zero previous failures is the average, yet in your specific combination of circumstances the model sees the complete lack of any prior academic setbacks as a warning sign rather than a strength. 

The second most important influence is that you are not receiving extra educational support at school. This choice works against you in the model’s eyes, pulling the prediction further toward failure. Only 3.4% of students who ultimately passed had no school support, so your situation stands out.

Third, although you have a clear desire to pursue higher education, the model still sees this ambition as slightly increasing the risk of failure in your case. This is the only one of the top three factors that mildly pushes toward passing, but its helpful effect is smaller than the other two influences.

To improve, you should seriously consider accepting the remedial courses, actively seeking extra academic help, and turning your ambition for higher education into a concrete study plan that includes more structured weekly study time and fewer absences. Addressing these areas now can reduce your risk and help you succeed. (248 words)
